title: PHD2 Guiding settings has no way to test the connection -- the one integration you cannot verify
summary: The headline claim (no Test affordance) was already closed by wave 4, which added a 'Test connection' row calling GuidingBackend.isPhd2Running. What survived was what wave 4 explicitly fenced off in its own caveat ('No PHD2 version or profile readout: the bridge exposes api_phd2_get_profile but no GuidingBackend method does, and wiring it would mean changing the role interface plus all three backend implementations') -- which is exactly the ownership excuse this wave is told not to repeat. Worse, the wave-4 row printed 'PHD2 answered on localhost:4400.' off a bare TCP connect, which proves only that *some* process holds 4400: a claim the probe never established. Built the real handshake instead. New packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/phd2_probe.dart opens PHD2's event server, reads the `Version` event PHD2 sends unprompted to every connecting client (giving PHDVersion/PHDSubver), then makes one read-only `get_profile` JSON-RPC call for the active equipment profile, and reports one of four honest outcomes: identified / unidentified (socket opened, nothing claimed to be PHD2) / unreachable / reachableUnverified (master too old for the endpoint). Wired through GuidingBackend.phd2Probe -> FFI backend (host-local Dart socket, the FFI backend runs on the imaging host), NetworkBackend (GET /api/phd2/probe with a 404 degrade that reports reachableUnverified rather than inventing a version), DisconnectedBackend, and a new headless GET /api/phd2/probe handler + route + endpoint catalog entry. The Settings page now renders 'PHD2 2.6.13 answered on localhost:4400. Active profile: Main rig.' and gives the unidentified case a warning glyph instead of rounding it to pass or fail. No Rust change and no frb codegen needed -- PHD2's protocol was the only thing missing, not a bridge call. Deliberately NOT built: a profile *selector* (changing PHD2's loaded profile) is a feature, not the finding; the finding's `expected` asked for the profile to be reported. Phd2Launcher and the Guiding screen's live connect state already existed (the verifier's location_wrong note) and were left alone; isPhd2Running is untouched so the launcher's port-poll semantics cannot regress.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/phd2_probe_test.dart -> 7 tests against a real loopback ServerSocket speaking PHD2 (version+profile handshake, dev subver, silent socket is NOT PHD2, PHD2 that ignores get_profile still yields a version, closed port, host normalisation, wire round-trip). packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/phd2_test_connection_test.dart -> 4 widget tests asserting rendered text ('PHD2 2.6.13 answered on localhost:4400. Active profile: Main rig.') and that an anonymous listener is never called PHD2. packages/skotiq_core/test/backend/network_backend_guiding_contract_test.dart -> 2 tests (wire decode; 404 degrade does not invent a version). apps/desktop/test/headless_api/guiding_handlers_test.dart -> 3 tests on GET /api/phd2/probe (forwards endpoint, defaults, fail-closed port). apps/desktop/test/headless_api/network_backend_contract_test.dart (pre-existing) enforces the route registration. Whole-package suites for the three packages touched: apps/desktop 1002/1002 pass; packages/skotiq_app and packages/skotiq_core run with `--exclude-tags golden` (what `melos run test` does -- melos.yaml:318 -- because the pixel baselines are host-specific and produce false diffs off the baseline host; running without that flag adds ~45 app + 1 core pixel-diff failures that have nothing to do with this change). skotiq_app: 2786/2786, All tests passed. skotiq_core: 5408 pass / 23 fail, none of them this fix -- 6 in services/import/nina_sequence_fidelity_test.dart (all SequenceImportValidationFailedException '1 blocking issue(s) [Wait Has No Time Set]' raised from sequence_importer.dart:347, a concurrent wave-5 sequence-validation change in a file this fix never touches; they reproduce with the same 6 names when that file is run alone) and 17 in services/imaging_service_test.dart, which passes 68/68 when run on its own -- the whole-suite cold-start flakiness already tracked as an open task.
revert_check: (1) Replaced the production call site in phd2_guiding_settings.dart -- `final probe = await ref.read(guidingBackendProvider).phd2Probe(host: host, port: port);` -- with wave 4's `isPhd2Running` call and its old message: 3 of 4 widget tests FAILED (version+profile, anonymous-listener, unreachable-cause). Restored -> 4/4 pass. (2) Changed phd2_probe.dart finish() from `outcome: version == null ? Phd2ProbeOutcome.unidentified : Phd2ProbeOutcome.identified` to a flat `outcome: Phd2ProbeOutcome.identified`: 'a socket that never identifies itself is not reported as PHD2' FAILED. Restored -> 7/7 pass. (3) Deleted the `socket.write(...get_profile...)` request line in phd2_probe.dart: 'a real PHD2 handshake yields the version and the active profile' FAILED. Restored -> 7/7 pass. (4) Deleted `HeadlessRoute(HttpMethod.get, '/api/phd2/probe', h.handlePhd2Probe)` from apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/routes/guiding_routes.dart: 2 tests in network_backend_contract_test.dart FAILED with Actual: Set:['GET /api/phd2/probe']. Restored -> all pass.
caveats: The `apiPhd2GetProfile` FRB binding the finding called out is still uncalled: it requires the app's persistent PHD2 client to already be connected, which a Settings-page test cannot assume, so the probe asks PHD2 directly over its own socket instead. Removing the dead binding would need a Rust change plus frb codegen, which this campaign forbids. Only the desktop GUI path was exercised against a real PHD2-shaped server (the loopback fake); no real PHD2 install was available, so the version string parsing is validated against PHD2's documented Version event rather than a live PHD2. A profile *selector* was not built -- the finding asked for the current profile to be reported, not changed. The finding's other proposed item, an 'Auto-detect - not found' status on the executable-path row matching the plate-solver page, is deliberately NOT built and the reason is not a fence: there is no host-side 'find PHD2 without launching it' capability. skotiq_imaging/src/phd2.rs launch_phd2() finds it by querying the Windows uninstall registry key (or a POSIX candidate list) and immediately spawning it, so a detection probe would need a new Rust entry point plus frb codegen, which this campaign forbids. A Dart-only version could only check the POSIX candidate paths, which would render 'Auto-detect - not found' on Windows where PHD2 is installed and working -- inverting the defect rather than fixing it. The existing subtitle 'Auto-detect (optional)' states an intent, not a result, so it is not currently telling the user anything untrue.

title: Onboarding's 'Regulated cooling' toggle never enables cooling; the camera runs at ambient every session
summary: Both halves of this finding were closed by an earlier wave, with tests, and I verified each by running them. (a) The wizard now ASKS: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/onboarding/steps/camera_defaults_step.dart:395-404 renders a 'Start cooling when the camera connects' SkotiqSwitchRow (label at :396) whose onChanged reaches setCameraDefaults(coolOnConnect:) at :161, and packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/onboarding_provider.dart:432 now writes `coolOnConnect: draft.coolOnConnect` instead of the hardcoded false the verifier found. Off by default, which is the deliberate summer-daytime-TEC behaviour the verifier defended. (b) The orphaned app_settings key -- which the verifier called 'the real defect here' -- is retired: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/database/default_settings.dart:144-155 lists 'cooling_behavior' in _retiredSettingKeys with the reason (no UI, no setter, no reader, yet shipped seeded 'On Connect' so every settings snapshot, .nsbackup and /api/settings payload announced automatic cooling the app never did), and schema_helpers.dart:1047 _pruneRetiredSettings() deletes it on every database open (wired from migration_strategy.dart:32, i.e. beforeOpen, not onCreate/onUpgrade, so an existing profile is cleaned too).
test: Ran the existing coverage rather than adding duplicates: packages/skotiq_core/test/database/retired_settings_prune_test.dart (3 tests: not seeded fresh, removed on open for an older build, cooling_behavior specifically), packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/onboarding_cool_on_connect_test.dart (4 tests: the wizard answer reaches the created profile, a set-point alone never arms the cooler, turning regulated cooling back off disarms it), packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/onboarding/camera_defaults_cool_on_connect_test.dart (the wizard asks and records the yes). All 8 pass.
revert_check: n/a -- no change made this wave. The closing evidence is cited by file:line above; the prior wave's own revert check covers it.
caveats: Nothing further to do. Note for the ledger: the finding's headline ('the switch is decorative') was over-called even before the fix -- the 'Regulated cooling' switch always gated and persisted default_cooling_temp; what was missing was the separate cool-on-connect question, which now exists.
